items.stem: Based on these results, which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

items.stimulus: A county health department surveyed 500 adults chosen at random from the county's residents. Of those surveyed, 38% reported getting a flu vaccine during the most recent season. The associated margin of error for this estimate is 4%.
items.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: It is plausible that between 34% and 42% of the 500 surveyed adults got a flu vaccine last season.
It is plausible that between 34% and 42% of all adults in the county got a flu vaccine last season.
It is not possible that more than 42% of all adults in the county got a flu vaccine last season.
About 4% of the surveyed adults likely gave incorrect answers about getting a flu vaccine last season.
items.explanation: The interval is $38\% - 4\% = 34\%$ to $38\% + 4\% = 42\%$. It estimates the proportion for the population that was sampled, which is all adults in the county. So it is plausible that between 34% and 42% of the county's adults were vaccinated.

C.why: You treated the interval as a hard boundary. A margin of error gives a plausible range, so values outside it are unlikely but still possible. 'Not possible' claims too much certainty.

D.why: You read the margin of error as the share of respondents who answered wrongly. It measures sampling variability: how far the estimate could plausibly be from the true county proportion.

items.stimulus: A health department randomly selected 200 of a city's 40,000 adult residents and recorded each person's daily fiber intake. The mean intake for the selected adults was 21 grams per day, with an associated margin of error of 3 grams per day. A dietary guideline recommends 25 grams per day.
items.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: Every adult in the city plausibly falls short of the 25-gram guideline by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
The mean intake of the 200 selected adults plausibly falls short of 25 grams by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
The mean intake of the city's adults falls short of the 25-gram guideline by exactly 4 grams per day.
The mean intake of the city's adults plausibly falls short of 25 grams by between 1 and 7 grams per day.
items.explanation: The plausible city mean runs from 21 − 3 = 18 to 21 + 3 = 24 grams. Its shortfall from 25 grams therefore runs from 25 − 24 = 1 to 25 − 18 = 7 grams, and that range describes the mean of the city's adults.

A.why: You applied the interval to every individual. It describes the mean intake. Some residents may meet the guideline and others may fall far below it.

B.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 200 adults were measured, so their mean is exactly 21 grams and their shortfall is exactly 4 grams.

C.why: You treated the estimate as exact. A shortfall of 4 grams comes from the sample mean, and the margin of error widens it to 1 to 7 grams.

items.stimulus: A seed lot contains 20,000 wheat seeds. An agronomist randomly selected 400 seeds from the lot and found that 85% of the selected seeds germinated under standard test conditions, with an associated margin of error of 4%. The seller claims that at least 90% of the seeds in the lot will germinate under these conditions.
items.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
choices: It is plausible that between 16,200 and 17,800 seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
It is plausible that at least 90% of the seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 324 and 356 of the 400 selected seeds germinated under these conditions.
It is plausible that between 16,320 and 17,680 seeds in the lot would germinate under these conditions.
items.explanation: The plausible range is 85% − 4% = 81% to 85% + 4% = 89% of the lot. As counts, that is 0.81 × 20,000 = 16,200 to 0.89 × 20,000 = 17,800.

B.why: You noticed that 90% is close to the estimate but didn't check it against the interval. The interval ends at 89%, so the seller's claim is not supported by the data.

C.why: You applied the interval to the sample. The 400 seeds were tested, so exactly 340 germinated. The margin of error describes the 20,000-seed lot.

D.why: You took 4% of the estimated 17,000 seeds (680) as the margin. The margin is 4 percentage points of the whole lot: 0.04 × 20,000 = 800 seeds.
